next: Fix the 041122 page-7 spill. The '12 twips of residue' theory is dead: the real cause is measured and it is 186 pt, not 1.2. Page 7 row 2 cell 2 is ONE paragraph (no w:br, no paras record) whose text is the six heading lines welded with SPACES by PdfToWord:8653, carrying the FIRST line's x as its inset (tcW 10636, ind 9452, so 1184 twips = 59.2 pt usable). The renderer lays that one paragraph out as TWENTY-SEVEN lines at 10 pt, y 23.4-293.4 = 270 pt, in a row whose w:trHeight declares 84.1 pt (1682 twips). The table therefore lays out ~186 pt taller than the 842 pt sheet, the last row (the Verification block) does not fit, w:cantSplit moves it to a new page, and 9 pages come out as 10. The fit guard is blind to this because spacingTw charges w:trHeight and never the wrap. Tried and ruled out this run: (a) one w:p per line of a welded cell in DocxWriter (shipped, no-op here - the cell text carries no newline), (b) joining cell lines with a newline at PdfToWord:8653 so that path fires (reverted: still 10 pages, page 7 went 99 -> 108 lines), (c) shaving w:trHeight (last run, 16746, still 10 pages). The next thing to try is the one the mechanism points at: a welded paragraph's inset must be the block's LEFTMOST line x, not the first line's - the heading's lines start at x 232-377 (centred) and 513 (right-aligned), so an inset of ~191 pt instead of 472.6 pt gives the paragraph ~340 pt of width and ~3 lines instead of 27. Measure page count with a render into an EMPTY directory - a render that can return a pre-existing file has already cost this pipeline one false fix.
